subject.title: Memory/QMD: isolate mcporter sidecars per agent

question: Should QMD permanently treat bare local stdio definitions as OpenClaw-owned per-agent MCPorter sidecars while retaining every customized or credential-bearing definition under the user's original MCPorter configuration and daemon identity?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but repository policy treats config discovery, fallback behavior, persisted sidecar paths, and daemon ownership as compatibility-sensitive product contracts that cannot be approved from tests alone.

options.title: Approve the ownership split
options.body: Confirm the generated-versus-external contract, then require an exact-head rebase and fresh install/upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Land only narrow environment isolation
options.body: Split out the mcporter child-environment regression fix and defer generated per-agent config and daemon ownership until the permanent contract is defined.

recommendation.title: Approve the ownership split
recommendation.body: Confirm the generated-versus-external contract, then require an exact-head rebase and fresh install/upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail connects this person most directly to review and landing of the existing QMD/MCPorter daemon and environment behavior.
